title: Blender Basics: Objects, Navigation, Render
goal: Complete the Blender Guru donut tutorial basics: add objects, navigate, render, and transform

milestones.goal: Delete the default cube and add a monkey mesh
milestones.done_when: The default cube is gone and a monkey (Suzanne) mesh is visible in the 3D viewport.
hints: Select cube, press X or Delete
milestones.teach: The Add menu (Shift+A) is how you insert new objects into your scene.

milestones.goal: Orbit around the scene using the middle mouse button
milestones.done_when: The 3D viewport shows the monkey from a different angle than the default front view.
hints: Hold and drag Middle Mouse Button
Use the navigation widget in the corner
milestones.teach: Orbiting lets you inspect your 3D model from any angle without moving the object itself.

milestones.done_when: The viewport shading shows a rendered appearance with lighting and shadows instead of flat solid colors.
hints: Top Right Corner > Rendered View Mode
milestones.teach: Rendered view shows how your scene will look in the final output with full lighting calculations.

milestones.goal: Pan the view using Shift + Middle Mouse Button
milestones.done_when: The viewport has shifted position, showing a different part of the scene without changing the viewing angle.
hints: Use the Move Tool from the navigation widget
milestones.teach: Panning slides the viewport sideways without rotating, useful for looking at objects outside your current view.

milestones.goal: Move the light object using the Move Tool
milestones.done_when: The light object has been repositioned in the 3D viewport from its original location.
milestones.teach: The G key activates the Move tool, letting you reposition any selected object in 3D space.

milestones.done_when: A rendered image appears in a new window or the render result is visible in the interface.
milestones.teach: F12 triggers a full render of your scene, producing the final image output.

milestones.goal: Switch to camera view and move the camera
milestones.done_when: The viewport is now showing the scene from the camera's perspective (camera view).
hints: Numpad 0 to switch to camera view
Select camera, press G to move it
milestones.teach: The camera determines what the viewer sees in the final render; Numpad 0 toggles camera view.

milestones.goal: Add a cone to the scene
milestones.done_when: A cone object is visible in the 3D viewport alongside the monkey.
milestones.teach: Primitive shapes like cones are building blocks you can combine to create more complex models.

milestones.done_when: The cone is visibly larger than its default size in the viewport.
hints: Press S key and drag mouse to scale
milestones.teach: The S key activates Scale mode, letting you resize the selected object proportionally.

milestones.goal: Rotate the cone to align with the monkey's head
milestones.done_when: The cone is rotated so it appears aligned with or positioned on the monkey's head.
hints: Press R key and drag to rotate
milestones.teach: The R key activates Rotate mode, allowing you to spin the object around its axes.
